stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks MEA To Issue Public Notice Inviting Compensation Claims From Families Of Indians Killed In Russia-Ukraine War
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks MEA To Issue Public Notice Inviting Compensation Claims From Families Of Indians Killed In Russia-Ukraine War
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to issue a public notice inviting compensation claims from families of Indian nationals who died while fighting in the Russia-Ukraine war as part of the Russian armed forces, noting that only six families had sought compensation despite 51 reported deaths.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi directed the MEA to provide assistance to the affected families in securing compensation from Russian authorities.
The Court also asked the Ministry to place on record the compensation amounts determined by the Russian authorities and the amounts actually paid to the families.
“It is obvious that the right to seek compensation needs to be apprised to the other family members of the victims.
We are informed that the MEA is contacting those families one by one to secure the necessary documents and information.
It might be advisable for the MEA to issue a public notice and invite claims and thereafter provide full assistance to those families in order to secure the compensatory benefits for them.
In this regard, we expect that if fresh status report we find by the MEA”, the Court observed.

The Court passed the order in a writ petition filed by family members of 26 Indian nationals who allegedly travelled to Russia in search of employment but were recruited into the Russian armed forces.
The petition raises allegations of deception and human trafficking in connection with the recruitment of Indians to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war.
On July 31, 2026, the Supreme Court directed the MEA to appoint a nodal officer to coordinate with the families of deceased and injured Indian nationals who had travelled to Russia.

The Court also directed the Ministry to arrange DNA tests to identify mortal remains, provide families with the procedure and documents required to claim compensation from Russian authorities, and ensure that pending compensation claims did not delay the handover of mortal remains.
It further directed the Legal Services.

stories.headline: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.title: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has once again unearthed a large-scale scheme to circumvent India’s prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan under “Operation Deep Manifest”. DRI detected the import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, with an estimated market value of around Rs. 30 crore. The consignments were routed through Colombo Port, Sri Lanka, and falsifying their origin by using fabricated certificates of origin and invoices issued by UAE-based entities. Acting on specific intelligence, DRI launched a coordinated, fortnight-long operation between 26 September and 11 October 2026, conducting searches at linked premises in Gandhidham, Adipur, Veraval, Panipat, Pune, Patiala, Delhi and Mumbai. Investigation revealed that nine importers had brought in the 295 containers through Mundra and Kandla ports since March 2026, in violation of the prohibition. Out of the total 295 containers detected, five containers carrying 140 MT of Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, valued at Rs. 24.41 lakh, have been seized at Kandla Port. In addition, sales proceeds amounting to Rs. 20.96 lakh held in the importers’ bank accounts have been seized. Preliminary investigation has uncovered a transnational network involving entities owned by Pakistani, UAE, Sri Lankan and Indian nationals. The network allegedly coordinated the shipments and supporting documentation to disguise the Pakistani origin of the goods. Fabricated invoices issued by Dubai-based firms were used to support the transactions. Significantly, Bills of Lading relating to the Pakistan–Sri Lanka leg of the shipments and customs declarations filed with Sri Lanka Customs expressly mentioned Pakistan as the country of origin and India as the final destination. The Certificates of Origin submitted by the importers were found to be fabricated. Four persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962: two proprietors/partners of importing firms, a Customs Broker’s G-card holder, and the owner of a Dubai-based supplier who had also established and operated an importing firm in his father’s name. In a similar crackdown last month, DRI seized over 362,000 kg of Pakistan-origin dry dates packed in 13 containers imported by a Mumbai-based firm at CFS Ambad, Nashik. These cases highlight the evolving methods used by transnational networks to circumvent India’s import prohibition on Pakistani origin goods through third-country routing, false declarations of origin, fabricated trade documents and opaque financial arrangements. DRI remains committed to identifying and dismantling such networks and safeguarding India’s economic and national security interests. Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Government of India imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 02.05.2025.

stories.headline: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.title: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.summary: India does not see any problems in its agreements with the United States, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday, playing down any suggestion that ties depend on who occupies the White House.Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Goyal was asked whether relations would improve after the tenure of the current US president. He said they were already “very good”. “I don’t see any problem in any agreements with the United States. It’s about trade, defence partnership, technology partnership, it’s our critical maintenance partnership and our people-to-people engagement,” he said, adding that Washington is India’s largest trading partner and will remain so in the years ahead.The relationship, Goyal said, will strengthen “irrespective of changes in political thinking” in either country. Drawing on economic, political and security imperatives, it is “a very safe relationship” that the rest of the world need not worry about, he added.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road ahead“I think the US and India have a very consequential relationship, and it’s only going to get better, irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US,” the commerce minister said further.Goyal said the pandemic exposed India’s vulnerability when critical supplies, including vaccines, failed to arrive. That experience prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for a self-sufficient India, including a push into semiconductors, given annual chip purchases of $130 billion to $150 billion.Self-reliance did not mean isolation, he stressed. India has signed preferential trade agreements with 38 developed nations in the past four and a half years, he said, raising the GDP covered by such pacts to $70 trillion from $10 trillion before 2014. Talks are under way with Canada, Mexico, the Gulf Cooperation Council, Eurasia, Mercosur, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) and others, which could take coverage to about $85 trillion of a $115 trillion global total.Also Read: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?Trust was the key ingredient, he said, describing India’s aim as “a fair mix of efficiency amongst friends and self-sufficiency for critical elements”. India is now largely self-sufficient in food and energy, he said.On China, Goyal said India was open to engagement provided it gets a fair deal, continuity and geopolitical stability, adding that “the last word has not yet been scripted.”

Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Goyal was asked whether relations would improve after the tenure of the current US president.

The relationship, Goyal said, will strengthen “irrespective of changes in political thinking” in either country.
Drawing on economic, political and security imperatives, it is “a very safe relationship” that the rest of the world need not worry about, he added.

“I think the US and India have a very consequential relationship, and it’s only going to get better, irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US,” the commerce minister said further.
Goyal said the pandemic exposed India’s vulnerability when critical supplies, including vaccines, failed to arrive.
That experience prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for a self-sufficient India, including a push into semiconductors, given annual chip purchases of $130 billion to $150 billion.
Self-reliance did not mean isolation, he stressed.

India has signed preferential trade agreements with 38 developed nations in the past four and a half years, he said, raising the GDP covered by such pacts to $70 trillion from $10 trillion before 2014.

Talks are under way with Canada, Mexico, the Gulf Cooperation Council, Eurasia, Mercosur, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) and others, which could take coverage to about $85 trillion of a $115 trillion global total..
India is now largely self-sufficient in food and energy, he said.
On China, Goyal said India was open to engagement provided it gets a fair deal, continuity and geopolitical stability, adding that “the last word has not yet been scripted.”

stories.headline: Cabinet clears ₹53,428 cr. for social assistance programme till 2030-31, drops ‘Indira Gandhi’ from pension scheme names
stories.title: Cabinet clears ₹53,428 cr. for social assistance programme till 2030-31, drops ‘Indira Gandhi’ from pension scheme names
stories.summary: Critics question fixed five-year allocation for social pensions, saying it fails to account for rising beneficiary numbers and inflation
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) approved an outlay of ₹53,428 crore for the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with revised eligibility criteria and assistance rates for disability pension beneficiaries.
The scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana', while its pension and family benefit components will also be renamed, according to an official statement.
Under the revised norms, monthly assistance under the disability pension scheme will be ₹375 for beneficiaries aged up to 79 years and ₹625 for those aged 80 years and above.
The benchmark disability requirement for availing of the pension has been reduced from 80% to 40%.
The minimum age criterion has also been removed, making persons with disabilities eligible for assistance from birth.

The revised eligibility criteria, beneficiary coverage and assistance rates under the disability pension scheme will be implemented within three months of the issuance of guidelines, the statement read.
The pension schemes for the elderly and widows, along with the National Family Benefit Scheme, will continue in their existing form.
The Cabinet's approval is expected to benefit 3.20 crore beneficiaries across all 36 States and Union territories.

The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana', while the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme will be called the 'Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana'.

The Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme will be renamed the 'Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana', and the National Family Benefit Scheme will become the 'Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana'.
Launched on August 15, 1995, the NSAP provides assistance to poor households as part of the Centre's responsibility under Article 41 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution.
The Centre provides 100% central assistance under the programme to ensure uniform availability of support to beneficiaries across the country.

stories.headline: Owaisi moves Supreme Court on SIR, seeks anti-BJP alliance in Uttar Pradesh
stories.title: Owaisi moves Supreme Court on SIR, seeks anti-BJP alliance in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Owaisi moves Supreme Court on SIR, seeks anti-BJP alliance in Uttar Pradesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: AIMIM has challenged the SIR process in the Supreme Court while pursuing an opposition alliance in Uttar Pradesh.
Owaisi says both efforts are crucial to protect voting rights and prevent another BJP government.

AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday said his party had filed a petition and a review petition in the Supreme Court over the SIR process, questioning whether the Election Commission's decisions were unanimous and whether statutory forms had been changed.
Owaisi also said AIMIM was pursuing alliances ahead of next year's Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third term.
He also spoke about protests against SIR, Starlink's satellite communication services and the removal of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.
Owaisi said the Election Commission was required by law to work collectively, but it was not known whether its decisions were unanimous or whether any member had dissented.
"We filed the review petition also because the Supreme Court upheld SIR.
We were petitioners in the Bihar SIR case.
It is not understood whether the statutory form for enumeration has been changed.
We don't have any material.
We filed a detailed petition in the Supreme Court," he told reporters.
He said no other party in Telangana had matched AIMIM's efforts during the SIR process over the past three months.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Must Revisit Verdict Upholding SIR: Justice Abhay Oka
stories.title: Supreme Court Must Revisit Verdict Upholding SIR: Justice Abhay Oka
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Supreme Court must rethink its May 2026 judgment upholding the constitutionality of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, particularly when the process permits deletion of voters merely for not submitting the pre-filled enumeration forms, said former apex court judge Justice Abhay Oka.
"On this very ground itself, the Supreme Court must revisit its judgment...
The law clearly says that there can either be an intensive revision or a partial one...
Even for intensive revision under section 21(3), the law says that revision can be done only of a given constituency at one time and not all the constituencies simultaneously...
It also says that the revision must be done prior to general elections," Justice Oka said.
Another reason for revisiting this judgment is the enumeration form, which has been brought into existence by the Election Commission of India (ECI), without any power.
"The guidelines issued by the ECI says if someone doesn't fill the enumeration form, then their names will be deleted from the draft list...
This, according to me, is illegal...
This isn't a provision even under the Act of 1950 or even the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
A person must be removed from the list as per the law only...
And the law says, one can be removed only under section 21, which permits issuing a show cause notice to a voter and then after giving a hearing, deciding the case," Justice Oka said.
Justice Oka said that the enumeration form is not as per law and thus, if voters do not fill the same, their names cannot be deleted from the list.

stories.title: Supreme Court grants Sanjay Sureka bail in Rs 6,210-crore laundering case
stories.summary: Supreme Court grants Sanjay Sureka bail in Rs 6,210-crore laundering case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court granted Sanjay Sureka bail in the money laundering case.
The bench cited a lengthy trial while imposing strict safeguards against interference.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday granted bail to industrialist Sanjay Sureka, owner of Concast Steel and Power Limited, in a money laundering case involving alleged proceeds of crime worth Rs 6,210.72 crore.
The court said the trial would take considerable time as thousands of pages of documents had to be considered and around 98 witnesses examined.
It ordered Sureka's release subject to conditions imposed by the trial court.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said, "The appellant must not be subjected to the rigours of custody as long as the trial is pending.
Hence, the appellant must be released on bail, subject to furnishing of bail bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to such other terms and conditions as may be imposed by it."
The Supreme Court directed Sureka to deposit his passport with the trial court and not leave the country while the trial is pending without its prior permission.
It also barred him from attempting to influence witnesses or tamper with evidence while on bail.
The trial court may cancel his bail if he breaches any of the conditions, the bench said.
According to the complaint, Sureka fraudulently inflated the company's turnover to secure substantial bank credit and diverted funds through shell companies.
The Supreme Court's order said the alleged proceeds of crime amounted to Rs 6,210.72 crore.

stories.summary: India's wholesale price index-based inflation surged to 11.39% in September due to higher food, manufactured items, and energy prices. Wholesale inflation has risen significantly amidst global commodity inflation linked to the ongoing West Asia conflict. The rising costs have impacted various aspects of the economy, including the manufacturing sector and consumer prices. Retail inflation also increased to 5.54%, marking its highest level in 23 months.

event term: 'market regulator' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has backed its restrictions on Rajesh Exports Ltd and its managing director Rajesh Mehta, directing them to cooperate with an ongoing investigation into the company’s financial disclosures and transactions, while barring Mehta from dealing in the company’s securities until further orders.
In a confirmatory order issued on Wednesday, Sebi said the company and Mehta must provide documents, information and explanations sought by the investigating authority.

Rajesh Exports must also ensure truthful, accurate and complete disclosures in its financial statements, related-party transactions and other material information under applicable securities regulations.
The regulator directed a newly appointed forensic auditor to complete its work expeditiously and asked the investigating authority to conclude its probe without delay.
The directions took immediate effect and will remain in force until further orders.
The order follows an interim order dated 3 June, which raised concerns over the company’s financial reporting, disclosures and cooperation with the investigation.
The regulator said its prima facie findings indicate that Rajesh Exports overstated and misrepresented the group’s operational scale and financial performance between FY21 and FY25.
It alleged that about ₹15.15 trillion, or 99.8% of revenue attributed to the company’s subsidiaries during the period, was misrepresented.
The order flagged a significant disparity between Rajesh Exports’ consolidated revenue and the standalone revenue reported by its Swiss subsidiary, Valcambi SA.
For the five-year period from financial year 2020-21 to 2024-25, the company’s consolidated revenue was ₹15.45 trillion, while Valcambi’s standalone revenue was ₹3,027.38 crore.

Sebi said the difference raised concerns about the verifiability and reliability of the consolidated financial disclosures considering that about 97-99% of the company’s consolidated revenue was reported to originate from overseas subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries.
Sebi also flagged inconsistencies in submissions made during the investigation.

stories.headline: Delhi Protest | Section 172 BNSS Unconstitutional, Enables Arbitrary Detention By Police: Plea In Supreme Court
stories.title: Delhi Protest | Section 172 BNSS Unconstitutional, Enables Arbitrary Detention By Police: Plea In Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A petition filed in the Supreme Court has challenged the constitutional validity of Section 172 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 (erstwhile section 144 of CrPC) contending that the provision empowers police officers to detain or remove people for disregarding their directions without adequate safeguards against arbitrary action.

Filed by B.Tech student Samriddhi Das, the writ petition seeks a declaration that Section 172 violates Articles 14, 19 and 21, which guarantee equality before law, fundamental freedoms and protection of life and personal liberty.

The petition argues that the provision allows detention on the basis of a police officer's subjective assessment, without requiring reasonable apprehension of a cognizable offence, recorded reasons or adequate safeguards for judicial scrutiny.

“The Petitioner(s) submit that, taken together, these measures amount to a prior restraint on a peaceful, announced demonstration against a public authority; that they fail the test of proportionality; and that Section 172 BNSS, to the extent it enables en masse detention on the subjective satisfaction of the police, is manifestly arbitrary and violates Articles 14, 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b), 19(1)(d) and 21”, the plea states.
Section 172(1) BNSS requires people to comply with lawful directions issued by a police officer in the discharge of duties under Chapter XII, which deals with preventive action by the police.

Section 172(2) empowers a police officer to detain or remove anyone who resists, refuses, ignores or disregards such a direction, and either take the person before a Magistrate or release them as soon as possible within 24 hours in petty cases.
The petition contends that the provision had no counterpart in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and leaves crucial terms, including “lawful directions”, “remove” and “petty cases”, undefined.

According to the petition, the absence of clear limits on the directions police may issue and the circumstances in which a person may be detained creates the potential for arbitrary and discriminatory enforcement.

The plea arises from the police action during the protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10 against the Chief Election Commissioner in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The petition contends that thousands of people, including students, activists, lawyers, journalists and political leaders, were detained or prevented from reaching the protest site, including persons intercepted far from the area and some removed from trains.
The petitioner states that she was travelling to the protest but could not reach the site because of the restrictions imposed by the authorities.
The petition also challenges prohibitory measures under Section 163 BNSS, the closure of Metro stations, cancellation of trains and suspension of mobile internet in parts of Delhi.

stories.headline: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.title: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.summary: ‘At present, only persons purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has issued a mandatory directive that tickets sold across counters at every railway station nationwide must include travel insurance coverage identical to online bookings.
A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed the railway authorities to put the order into effect from October 27, 2026.
The order explicitly warned that failure to implement this mechanism would place direct liability squarely on the Railway Board.
“At present, only people purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount.

The court had granted sufficient time to the authorities to devise a mechanism extending such coverage to persons belonging to the lowest strata of society, who, in most cases, purchase their tickets at the railway reservation counters while undertaking journeys by train,” the court observed, pointing out that the railway had made no progress on providing insurance cover to all passengers.
The direction was based on a writ petition filed in the aftermath of the June 2023 Odisha train accident.
The petition initially focused on an independent probe into the accident and the implementation of safety systems like Kavach.

However, the court widened the scope of the case to include various passenger and infrastructural aspects of rail travel, including the lack of insurance for economically disadvantaged passengers who purchase tickets over the counter at stations.

The court, in its order dated October 6, recorded its “utter disappointment and displeasure at the conduct of the officers of the Ministry of Railways in such a serious matter concerning the safety of the common man”.
“The Railways have been representing before this court that all necessary steps are being taken in this regard.
However, it appears that such assurances have remained largely on paper and that no substantial change has taken place on the ground,” the court noted.
In a scathing order, the bench said even the budgetary provisions for the targeted areas relating to the safety of the common man and the prevention of untoward incidents had not been fully utilised.

stories.headline: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
stories.title: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
stories.summary: The Bench also quashed a U.P. Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Abhishek Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) made absolute the interim protection granted to independent journalist Abhishek Upadhyay from coercive action in a road rage case, as well as any subsequent First Information Reports.
Mr. Upadhyay had authored investigative online stories of the alleged misappropriation and theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple.
A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi also quashed an Uttar Pradesh.
Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Mr. Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident.
The court found the police version that the data was sought to trace/arrest the petitioner “somewhat in contradiction” with the contents of its notice to the platform.
The court termed the notice an “overkill”, and said any information received by the police pursuant to the notice would not be used against the journalist.
The “arrest of the petitioner (Mr. Upadhyay) shall remain stayed till further notice,” the court said.
It made absolute its interim orders of August 25 and September 7, which had protected him from arrest and directed him to cooperate with the investigation, respectively.
The copy of the road rage FIR had been supplied to the petitioner, the court noted.
The Bench ordered that Mr. Upadhyay could challenge the road rage FIR on any grounds.
The apex court has not commented on the merits of the case.

The court allowed Mr. Upadhyay, who said the road rage case was “staged”, to counter his online reports about the temple, and the liberty to file a separate petition seeking guidelines to protect digital privacy and journalistic freedoms.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves ₹2,010 cr bonus for over 11 lakh railway employees
stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹2,010 cr bonus for over 11 lakh railway employees
stories.summary: The payment of PLB, which is disbursed each year before the Durga Puja/Dusshera holidays, acts as an incentive to motivate the railway employees
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Ahead of Dussehra and Deepavali festivals, the Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Productivity Linked Bonus of 78 days for 11,40,770 railway employees, amounting to ₹2009.61 crore.

The payment of PLB, which is disbursed each year before the Durga Puja/Dusshera holidays, acts as an incentive to motivate the railway employees for working towards improvement in the performance of the Railways, the government said.
“The maximum amount payable per eligible railway employee is ₹17,951 for 78 days,” it added.

The bonus will be paid to various categories of Railway staff like track maintainers, loco pilots, train managers (Guards), station masters, supervisors, technicians, technician helpers, pointsmen, ministerial staff and other Group C staff.
“The performance of Railways in the year 2025-26 was very good.
Railways loaded a record cargo of 1670 million tonnes and carried nearly 7.41 billion Passengers,” it said.
